description: Consolidate the two scraping stacks into one (docs/UNIFIED-PROJECT-PLAN.md §6): fold the parallel/legacy TS *-scraper.ts stack (~14.3k LOC, ~29 files) into the Python pinakes_engine acquisition layer, so there is ONE async fetch layer, ONE rate-limiter/politeness policy, ONE cache, and ONE set of domain adapters. This is where 'incredibly fast at AI-powered scraping' is actually won — the levers the benchmark showed matter (concurrency, caching, parsing), not the language.

userStories.title: Map + migrate the TS domain scrapers onto the engine's acquire layer
userStories.description: Inventory the TS *-scraper.ts / *-enrichment.ts modules, identify which domains they cover vs the engine's existing adapters, and reimplement each on the engine's async HTTP + rate-limit + cache infrastructure. Deduplicate against existing engine adapters rather than porting 1:1.
acceptanceCriteria: Every TS scraper's capability is available through the Python engine acquisition layer (no domain regressed).
All acquisition uses the engine's single rate-limited/cached async HTTP client and shared parsing utilities; no scraper keeps its own ad-hoc fetch loop.
Acquisition parity: representative fetch+parse for each migrated domain yields the same normalized rows as before (on cached fixtures).

userStories.title: One concurrency + politeness model, benchmarked
userStories.description: Ensure the unified acquisition layer runs fetches concurrently with per-host rate limiting and caching, and record a quick before/after throughput note so the speed goal is evidenced (network-bound reality per the plan).
acceptanceCriteria: Concurrent multi-source acquisition is supported with per-host politeness preserved (min_interval honored per host, not globally serialized).
A short benchmark note (docs/) shows end-to-end acquisition throughput for a representative job and confirms where time goes (network vs parse).
